record_identity.title: Anthropic withheld Claude Mythos 5.1 from UK AISI pre-release evaluation

incident_identity.historical_event_name: 2026 Anthropic Mythos 5.1 UK AISI pre-release evaluation withholding
incident_identity.date_basis: The Financial Times reported on 9 September 2026 that Anthropic had not provided Claude Mythos 5.1 to the UK AI Security Institute for pre-release testing. Anthropic launched Mythos 5.1 on 1 September 2026. The exact date on which Anthropic decided not to provide pre-release access is not established in the reviewed public evidence; 9 September is therefore used as the public reporting anchor rather than an asserted decision date.

summary: The Financial Times reported that Anthropic did not provide Claude Mythos 5.1 to the United Kingdom's AI Security Institute for pre-release evaluation before the model's 1 September 2026 launch, describing the episode as the first time Anthropic had withheld its latest major model from AISI in this way. Anthropic describes Mythos 5.1 as its newest Mythos-class model with gains in cybersecurity and biology and says access is currently limited to a small set of vetted United States organisations. AISI had previously evaluated Anthropic's Mythos Preview and documented substantial autonomous cyber capability. The occurrence therefore records the loss of a previously available independent pre-release evaluation pathway for a high-capability frontier model; it does not establish that Mythos 5.1 is unsafe or that Anthropic breached any legal or contractual duty.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The Financial Times reports that Anthropic withheld Claude Mythos 5.1 from UK AISI pre-release testing and that UK officials viewed the loss of access as a national-security and strategic concern. Anthropic's own Mythos page confirms that Mythos 5.1 launched on 1 September 2026, has gains in cybersecurity and biology, and is currently available only to a small set of vetted US organisations. AISI's public evaluation of the earlier Mythos Preview establishes that AISI had previously tested Anthropic's frontier cyber model and found significant improvements in autonomous cyber capability, including completion of a multi-stage simulated network attack. Together, these sources establish a change in external pre-release access and the material safety-assurance context, while not establishing Anthropic's internal motive for the decision.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence is an institutional assurance and access-governance failure surface rather than evidence of model misconduct. Independent frontier-model evaluation depends on evaluators receiving timely access before deployment or restricted release. Where an external national safety institute that previously evaluated a provider's frontier models no longer receives pre-release access, the state's ability to independently characterize capability, validate safeguards and identify weaknesses before use is reduced. The governance issue is therefore the interruption of an established assurance pathway and the dependence of national safety oversight on provider-controlled and potentially geopolitically constrained model access.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: For CAM, the incident is relevant to sovereign assurance, cross-border AI governance and the difference between voluntary provider cooperation and durable independent oversight capability. A national safety institute cannot independently evaluate a frontier model it cannot access. The case therefore illustrates how frontier-model availability, export controls, provider policy and geopolitical relationships can become operational dependencies for public-sector safety assurance even without any proven defect in the model itself.
assessment_boundaries: This record does not conclude that Claude Mythos 5.1 is unsafe, inadequately safeguarded or responsible for any harmful deployment outcome.

The reviewed public evidence does not establish that Anthropic acted at the direction of the United States government or that US protectionism was the cause of the decision; those propositions are reported concerns and interpretations rather than established motive.
The record does not assert that Anthropic had a legal, contractual or regulatory duty to provide Mythos 5.1 to UK AISI before release.

The Financial Times characterisation that this was the first time Anthropic withheld its latest major model from AISI is preserved as source-attributed reporting rather than independently reconstructed historical fact.
The occurrence concerns loss of pre-release independent evaluation access; it does not establish that no post-release evaluation, information sharing or subsequent cooperation will occur.

observed_values.qualitative_value: Anthropic launched Mythos 5.1 on 1 September 2026 and states that access is limited to a small set of vetted US organisations. FT reported the AISI non-submission on 9 September. AISI's earlier Mythos Preview evaluation found that the model completed its 32-step simulated corporate-network attack from start to finish in 3 of 10 attempts; this figure is contextual evidence about prior Mythos capability, not a measurement of Mythos 5.1.

dimensions.assessment_basis: The preserved sources establish the bounded consequence described in the Incident summary: The Financial Times reported that Anthropic did not provide Claude Mythos 5.1 to the United Kingdom's AI Security Institute for pre-release evaluation before the model's 1 September 2026 launch, describing the episode as the first time Anthropic had withheld its latest major model from AISI in this way. Anthropic describes Mythos 5.1 as its newest Mythos-class model with gains in cybersecurity and biology and says access is currently limited to a small set of vetted United States organisations. AISI had previously evaluated Anthropic's Mythos Preview and documented substantial autonomous cyber capability. The occurrence therefore records the loss of a previously available independent pre-release evaluation pathway for a high-capability frontier model; it does not establish that Mythos 5.1 is unsafe or that Anthropic breached any legal or contractual duty. Unreported downstream consequences were not inferred.
